name: Rename a local variable — preserves test pass/fail
description: Given a Python function `def area(w, h): return w * h`, rename `w` to `width` and `h` to `height`. Assert the test suite still passes and the output is identical.

input.source: def area(w, h): return w * h

verification: All existing tests pass with exit code 0
Function signature changed to (width, height) — verify by inspection
No logic changes — diff shows only identifier renames

name: Extract function — behaviour unchanged
description: Given a monolithic function containing a loop that sums squares, extract the loop body into a helper function `square(x)` and call it. Assert the output and tests are unchanged.
verification: New helper function `square(x)` exists and is called from the original
All existing tests pass with exit code 0
The original function's output for the same input is identical

name: Move a file — imports updated, tests pass
description: Given a module `src/utils/helpers.py` imported by `src/app.py`, move the helpers to `src/lib/helpers.py` and update all import paths. Assert the application still runs and all tests pass.

file_structure.tests/test_app.py:
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'src')
from src.app import greet  # indirect test

expected_behavior: Move completed, all imports updated, all tests pass
verification: All import statements updated to src.lib.helpers
All existing tests pass with exit code 0

name: Rename a public API — deprecation shim keeps callers working
description: Given a class `Calculator` with method `compute()`, rename it to `evaluate()` while keeping `compute()` as a deprecated alias that delegates to `evaluate()`. Assert the old name still works with a deprecation warning, and new code uses the new name.
expected_behavior: Old callers work with deprecation warning, new callers use the new name
verification: Old API `compute()` raises a DeprecationWarning when called
Old API still returns the correct result
New API `evaluate()` works without any warning
All existing tests pass with exit code 0

name: Reject refactor that changes behaviour
description: Given a function with a known bug where the refactorer attempts to fix the bug during the same change. Assert that the refactor process catches the behaviour change (tests that captured the buggy behaviour now fail, or verification detects the logic diff).
expected_behavior: Refactor is rejected — test fails OR diff shows logic change
verification: Executing the 'refactored' code causes at least one test to fail
OR diff-checking reveals a logic branch change (not just structural)
The refactorer is directed to either revert or separate the bugfix into its own commit
